endorsements.quote: Autonomously monitoring the fidelity of RL algorithms for intervention delivery is important for detecting, alerting, and preventing issues such as those presented above.
Once these issues are identified, an automated notification system (e.g., automated email) can alert the monitoring team when an issue occurs.

unlisted_practices: Identify potential issues in online AI decision-making algorithms and categorize them by severity (red, yellow, green) before deployment.
Develop pre-specified fallback methods that default to baseline functionality when action selection or learning fails.
Flag and exclude incorrect or corrupted data from online algorithm updates, and continue using the most recent decision rules if an update fails.
Document all incident details, including timestamps, impacted participants, and fallback used, and pass them to data analysts to adjust post-deployment analyses.
Establish agreements among all development teams before deployment clarifying responsibilities for documenting issues.

screen.reason: This paper presents guidelines and a framework for monitoring online AI decision-making algorithms and deploying fallback safeguards in just-in-time adaptive interventions (JITAIs), illustrated via two case studies.
